data.title: South Korea, China, Taiwan regulators step in to rescue stock markets - Here are the steps they are taking
data.description:
Stock market regulators in China, Taiwan, and South Korea are stepping up to curb the fallout from the sell-off witnessed in Wall Street's AI trade, which has taken the Nasdaq 100 index into "bear market territory" and the Dow Jones and S&P 500 into a "technical correction".

Markets in all the three countries are steeply below the peaks they had surged to in the first half of the year, as the AI trade unwound, and concerns were raised over the financials of many companies.

Here are the steps regulators are taking to prevent any further fallout:

China

In China, the minimum margin requirement for investors buying securities with borrowed funds will fall to 80% from 100% on November 30, as per a notice issued by the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing stock exchanges, with approvals from the China Securities Regulatory Commission. The figure was raised to 100% in January to curb excess leverage risks.

According to the Xinhua news agency citing the regulator, the measure could unlock additional funds worth $60 billion.

The CSI 300 index has also slumped into a bear market after a 8% fall in October, marking its worst monthly performance in more than a decade, as economic weakness and a sharp fall in tech shares weighed.

Earlier this month, the People's Bank of China had said that it will conduct more than 100 billion yuan worth of swap operations to provide liquidity to securities firms, fund managers, and insurers, along with a relending program for share buybacks and stake increases, the interest rate for which was cut to 1% from 1.25% earlier.

South Korea

The poster boy of the Asia-Pacific AI trade also announced phased measures to calm the markets down amidst rising volatility.

Moves announced by the Korean authorities include ensuring a stock stabilization fund to be put in place to respond when needed. The move was announced by top financial officials on Sunday after an emergency meeting.

According to analysts, the government is preparing a 10 trillion won market stabilization fund, although the size looks insufficient to materially change the near-term sentiment.

Despite the measures, the KOSPI is down another 3% on Monday morning, while the Japanese stock markets are shut on account of a holiday.

"A sustained return to tech likely requires clearer resolution of Nvidia-related uncertainty, evidence that AI demand remains resilient despite tighter US chip export to China, and geopolitical easing that brings oil meaningfully lower," Shawn Oh of NH Investment & Securities said.

Taiwan

Over the weekend, Taiwan also announced a blanket ban on short-selling in stocks below their previous day's closing price. The Taiwanese TAIEX fell 18% last week, to mark its worst weekly fall since 1991.

The regulator also said that they have been buyers in stocks and urged investors to keep calm amidst the sell-off.

data.title: Two Chinese copper smelters blend concentrate overseas to boost supply, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • China Minmetals starts overseas blending on trial basis in third quarter, sources say
  • China Copper has engaged in overseas blending for around one year, sources say
  • CRU pegs global copper concentrate deficit at 289,000 metric tons this year

Two large Chinese smelters have begun blending copper concentrate at a Malaysian port in a bid to boost supply amid a worsening feedstock shortage, four people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

China is by far the world's largest copper ore processor. But its rules strictly limit the allowable levels of toxins such as arsenic, meaning that only about one-fifth of concentrate produced outside the country meets import standards.

Blending higher-standard concentrate grades with those containing more toxins can allow more concentrate volumes to meet Chinese regulations. China, however, limits the number of different concentrates that can be blended domestically.

So, in order to broaden the availability of supply that can be processed in China, integrated producer China Minmetals Nonferrous Metals and smelter China Copper have been blending complex copper concentrate containing high impurities in Port Klang, Malaysia, the people said.

China Copper has engaged in overseas blending for around a year, while China Minmetals started doing so on a trial basis in the third quarter of this year, two of the people said.

It was not immediately clear how much copper concentrate the two smelters have blended in the Malaysian port.

China Minmetals and China Copper did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The blending of complex copper concentrates has been allowed in bonded zones at domestic ports since 2020 and currently takes place at ports including Dalian, Yantai and Fangcheng.

However, blending overseas provides flexibility to mix several different types of concentrate while more stringent requirements apply for blending domestically, said one of the people.

International trading houses have long blended concentrates at ports outside China to meet its import standards. The overseas blending by the two Chinese smelters, however, has not been previously reported.

All the people requested anonymity as the information is not public.

The copper concentrate shortage worsened this year as smelting capacity expanded and disruptions reduced mined supply, driving unexpectedly high production cuts in China in the fourth quarter.

Consultancy CRU pegged the global copper concentrate deficit at 289,000 metric tons this year, versus 2,000 tons in 2025. Analysts expect mined copper supply to improve in 2027, but not enough to fill the gap.

Global copper concentrate supply is projected to grow by 4% in 2027 following a 0.4% rise this year, according to CRU.

data.title: XPENG Launches Public Advanced ADAS Test Rides at Its Paris Store, Becoming the First Chinese Automaker to Offer the Experience Overseas
data.description:
Key points:
  • As the first Chinese automaker to introduce public advanced ADAS test rides at a European retail store, XPENG brings intelligent driving beyond industry showcases and closer to everyday consumers, joining Tesla as only one of two global automakers bringing advanced ADAS experiences to European consumers.
  • The initiative marks XPENG's first overseas retail-based intelligent driving test ride experience, building on its large-scale public debut at the 2026 Paris Motor Show.
  • Powered by XPENG's VLA 2.0 architecture, NGP is undergoing European testing and localisation ahead of its planned international rollout in 2027, subject to regulatory approval and market readiness.

PARIS, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, today announced the launch of public advanced ADAS test rides at its Paris store, marking its first overseas retail-based intelligent driving experience. The initiative makes XPENG the first Chinese automaker to offer public urban advanced ADAS test rides through a European retail location, bringing the technology closer to European consumers on real city roads.

Powered by XPENG's VLA 2.0 architecture, Next Generation Pilot (NGP) is an AI-powered advanced driver-assistance system designed to support drivers in complex, real-world driving scenarios. At the 2026 Paris Motor Show, XPENG and Tesla were the only two automakers globally to participate in the event's official Autonomous Lab programme, offering visitors the opportunity to experience advanced intelligent driving technology on real Paris roads. The Paris store initiative builds on this milestone, extending the experience beyond the motor show and bringing the technology closer to European consumers.

At XPENG's store at 10 boulevard Gouvion-Saint-Cyr in Paris, customers can book advanced ADAS test rides to experience NGP on real city roads, including dense urban traffic, complex intersections and other challenging driving environments. The experience gives European consumers a firsthand look at the capabilities of advanced intelligent driving in real-world conditions.

The Paris initiative comes as XPENG continues to test and localise its advanced driver-assistance technology for European road conditions and regulatory requirements, ahead of its planned international rollout in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and market readiness.

He Xiaopeng, Chairman & CEO of XPENG, said: “Our mission is to bring Physical AI into everyday life and make advanced intelligent driving accessible to users worldwide. At the Paris Motor Show, many people asked when they could experience our technology themselves. Today, we are taking that next step.

For us, this is not just about showcasing technology, but about understanding how people experience it in the real world. Backed by our full-stack R&D and continuous localisation efforts, we are committed to listening to European customers, adapting our technology to their needs, and working towards safer, smarter and more seamless mobility experiences. This is what ‘In Europe, For Europe, With Europe’ means to us.”

Romain Caubet, Country Manager of XPENG in France, said, “At the Paris Motor Show, we introduced European audiences to our advanced driving assistance technology through real-world demonstrations. Today, we are bringing that experience closer to customers through our Paris store. Paris offers a unique and challenging urban driving environment, making it an ideal location for people to experience the technology firsthand. We look forward to hearing their feedback as we continue to develop our intelligent driving experience for European customers.”

XPENG is also contributing to international discussions on automated driving through its role as OICA Secretary for the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) TF-ESRI taskforce.

Press Kit: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Kgb_VapslbWilhrR_r3zYKy8KbaxD2In

About XPENG

XPENG is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. This unified technology foundation of XPENG powers an expansive product portfolio of smart EVs, robotaxis, and humanoid robots, advancing the deployment of Physical AI at scale.

Headquartered in Guangzhou, China, XPENG is dual-primary listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. With global capabilities across R&D, manufacturing, sales, and services, XPENG drives continuous technological innovation and fosters an open Physical AI ecosystem, making life smarter, safer, and better for users worldwide. data.title: Zepp Health Corporation Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Unaudited Financial Results
data.description:
MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zepp Health Corporation () ("Zepp", the "Company" or "we") today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:

  • Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%.
  • Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments.
  • GAAP and adjusted net loss[1] attributable to Zepp were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million in the same period of 2025, and US$11.3 million and US$12.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. The net loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities.
  • As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million as of September 30, 2025 and US$106.3 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Product Innovation: Launched T-Rex Dual Solar, pairing a bright AMOLED display with solar charging through both the front of the watch and its glass-ceramic back. It offers up to 25 days of battery life under typical use, and its dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation are designed for multi-day trips outdoors.
  • Software Ecosystem: Rolled out Zepp OS 6 to more existing watch models and made HYROX post-race station analysis available on more models. These updates give customers more value from the devices they already own and help build confidence in Amazfit's ongoing support for its products.

[1] Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss) and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," said Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health. "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

In the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our new, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

Product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand."

Leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health, commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

We continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in new product launches, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026.

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

  • [2] Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Please refer to the section titled "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

  • [3] Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million and US$106.3 million as of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, respectively.

The Company recorded inventory of US$68.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with US$62.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and US$87.7 million as of September 30, 2025. We will continue to manage the inventory level tightly and working capital closely.

Long-term and short-term debt levels remained flat as of September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026. We remain committed to prudently managing our debt profile. Our primary objective is to maintain overall debt levels broadly stable while actively extending the maturity profile by replacing short-term borrowings with long-term debt. During the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we successfully converted US$26.6 million and US$56.5 million, respectively, of short-term debt into long-term obligations, and we expect to continue this strategy in the coming quarters, supported by sufficient financial headroom and liquidity capacity. Since the beginning of 2023, the Company has cumulatively retired US$38.1 million of debt, and will continue to optimize its capital structure.

Share Repurchase Program Update

The Company announced in its third quarter 2021 earnings release that the board had authorized a share repurchase program of up to US$20 million through November 2022. On November 21, 2022, the board authorized a 12-month extension of the Company's share repurchase program. On November 20, 2023, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. On November 18, 2024, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 24 months. On November 22, 2026, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. Pursuant to the extended share repurchase program, the Company may repurchase its shares in the form of ADSs and/or ordinary shares through November 2027 with an aggregate value equal to the remaining balance under the share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had used US$17.8 million to repurchase approximately 2.4 million ADSs. The Company expects to fund the repurchases under the extended share repurchase program out of its existing cash balance.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company's management currently expects net revenues to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, which would represent an increase by approximately 6% to 12% from US$85.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

This outlook is based on current market conditions and reflects the Company's current and preliminary estimates of market, operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to change.

data.title: Swap the Winter Wonderland for a Seaside Paradise: Agoda Picks Five Sun-Soaked Shores Across Asia
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Winter does not have to mean another week in the cold. Digital travel platform Agoda spotlights five sun-soaked shores across Asia where travelers can trade the winter wonderland for a seaside paradise - some in time for a late-afternoon swim, and one where travelers can fall asleep in winter and wake up on warm white sand.

Leave a cold morning in Seoul, Tokyo or Taipei behind. Ishigaki in Japan's far south and Kenting at Taiwan's southern tip offer spring-like days of about 21 to 26°C, while Langkawi, Panglao, and Koh Lanta bring the full tropical heat.

"Travelers still want to get away, but they also want to know they're getting good value," said Andrew Smith, Senior Vice President, Supply at Agoda. "We're seeing more of them look beyond the usual hotspots for short-haul trips that feel like a discovery - a quieter shore, the right season and experiences that go beyond the beach. At Agoda, our role is to help people find those escapes and make them easy to book."

Ishigaki, Yaeyama Islands, Japan

South of Okinawa's main island, the largest of Japan's subtropical Yaeyama Islands, Ishigaki brings a mild thaw rather than tropical heat, so pack a light layer and a wetsuit for longer swims. Glass-bottom boats glide over coral, giant clams, and tropical fish at Kabira Bay, snorkeling and diving trips head out to the reefs and turtles, and after dark the island's International Dark Sky Park gives some of Japan's clearest views of the winter sky. Nonstop flights take about three hours from Seoul and Tokyo and about an hour from Taipei, and travelers from Shanghai can connect via Taipei or Naha.

Panglao, Bohol, Philippines

Panglao is the overnight escape: fly out of Seoul or Busan after dark, land after midnight and wake up to a white-sand beach. A short boat ride away, the Balicasag Marine Sanctuary is known for its turtles and coral walls, whether one snorkels or dives. Just across the bridge on Bohol, the Chocolate Hills roll out from the viewing deck in Carmen, and the Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary in Corella offers a quiet look at the island's most famous primate.

Langkawi, Malaysia

For full tropical heat and a true dry season, Langkawi is the pick. Off Malaysia's northwest coast, it's one of the few parts of the country with a distinct dry spell from December to February. Ride the SkyCab up to the curved SkyBridge for sweeping views over the rainforest and the Andaman Sea, then take a boat through the mangroves and limestone cliffs of Kilim Karst Geoforest Park, part of Langkawi's UNESCO Global Geopark. A short hop of about an hour from Kuala Lumpur still puts travelers on the beach the same day.

Kenting, Southern Taiwan

Back on the milder side, Kenting at Taiwan's southern tip has the island's driest, sunniest winter. It's another spring-like escape, much like Ishigaki, and a world away from the cooler, cloudier north. Walk the grounds of Eluanbi Lighthouse, the "Light of East Asia," then follow the coral coast through Kenting National Park before evening brings snack stalls and a slow beach-town buzz to Kenting Street. Non-stop flights from Seoul, Tokyo, and Shanghai land in Kaohsiung, two to three hours by express bus or car from the coast, so travelers can still reach the shore the same day.

Koh Lanta, Thailand

On Thailand's Andaman coast, Koh Lanta rounds things out with a quieter take on the tropics. December to February is its classic dry season, and calm seas make for an easy boat trip to Koh Rok, where clear, shallow reefs are perfect for snorkeling in Mu Ko Lanta National Park. On Koh Lanta itself, the lighthouse at Laem Tanod looks out over the Andaman, and Lanta Old Town keeps a row of wooden stilt houses along the eastern shore. Fly into Phuket or Krabi and allow three to five hours by van, ferry or car. Travelers can book an early arrival to hit the beach the same day.

Travelers looking to book can also take advantage of Agoda's Mega Sale, which runs through 30 November. During the main sale, travelers can access hotel offers of up to 60% off. A Flash Sale on 27 November will feature selected offers of up to 70% off.

With over 6 million properties, more than 130,000 flight routes and a wide range of activities to choose from, travelers can discover and plan their next warm, sandy escape on Agoda.com or the Agoda app.

data.title: Battered Home Builders Turn to Remodeling and Repair Work to Pay the Bills — WSJ
data.description:
By Nicholas G. Miller

Bruce Rogers has made a good living developing lavish, seaside homes with double-decker balconies overlooking the North Carolina coast. His home-builder firm charges over $1 million to deliver them.

These days, the company spends much of its time on more mundane tasks, such as replacing the deck of an existing home for $25,000. It does a lot of siding and window replacement, too.

Home builders are contending with one of their toughest periods in years. Higher interest rates are driving away buyers. Many firms have to offer customers significant incentives. Rising construction costs have also weighed on industry sentiment, which this month sank to a 14-year low.

Consequently, many smaller-scale builders are pivoting to remodel and repair work — a market getting a boost from homeowners opting to renovate their homes rather than move during this extended slump in home sales.

Rogers recently had an agreement to build a $2.5 million house from the ground up. But the customers backed out, worried about the rise in mortgage rates and how tariffs and fuel surcharges would increase building costs over time.

"That's the kind of thing that's driving us to have to go into remodeling because people right now are just not looking at new construction," said Rogers, founder of Crystal Coast Construction Unlimited.

His company has increased its emphasis on remodeling on its website, featuring projects typically handled by smaller contractors.

At Diamond Custom Homes, in Naples, Fla., remodeling went from about one-third of its work to the majority in the first years after the housing market slowed in 2023. The company created a new remodeling architect role and has subcontractors solely focused on that business.

Meanwhile, White Maple Construction in New Jersey is currently planning its first custom home since it launched in 2020. It has been trying to expand into the market but has found people want to stay in their current homes given high mortgage rates and land prices.

"It's easier to just get the home you want by doing a big addition," said co-owner Ryan Brining.

The remodeling market overall is far from booming. Annual spending on home improvements and repairs has been largely flat in recent years and is expected to remain subdued through next year, the Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies said.

Repair and remodeling activity tends to sag when the housing market slows since many homeowners start new projects before selling or after buying a home.

But home-improvement retailers Home Depot and Lowe's say that homeowners are still undertaking smaller projects, which has allowed the companies to maintain sales growth in their business selling to construction professionals. Home Depot has recorded nine straight quarters of comparable sales growth for its business selling to people in the construction business.

And remodeling offers builders several advantages that the new-home market doesn't.

For one, homeowners are opting to stay in their current homes to keep their low mortgage rates. They can tap in to record levels of equity they have built up to pay for renovations.

Moreover, the median age of America's housing stock reached 43 years in 2025, according to the Census Bureau, up from 35 years in 2010. Many of these homes require major repairs and replacements to their roofing and plumbing systems.

And the aging baby boomers have created a surge in demand for accessible home renovations.

Jim Reif, a builder and remodeler in Wisconsin, said he has been doing projects to make bathrooms or entryways accessible for older people who are staying put.

"I think some of the people would be interested in having a newer place, but they're used to the interest rates at 2 and 3%," he said. "So they just decide to stay where they are."

Brittany Starr thought she would have long moved from her Maryland home that was too small for her husband and two children. But home values in their area had surged since they had first bought, making a move infeasible.

Instead, with the help of a home-equity line of credit, the family spent about $300,000 adding a master bath and bedroom on the main level and an additional bedroom and office space on the second floor.

"We never really expected to stay in this house for the rest of our lives, but we now are looking at our house as a long-term place to live," she said.

Homeowners are also doing less do-it-yourself work, increasingly turning to professionals. In 2023, the DIY share of total home-improvement spending fell to a record low of 16%, down from 27% in 2003. People these days place a premium on their own time, making them less willing to undertake projects themselves, said Rachel Bogardus Drew, director of the Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies Remodeling Futures Program.

Those factors make the remodeling market an attractive backup plan to builders, even though work on an existing home is far more complicated and unpredictable.

It can mean having to move around an existing chimney, opening up floors and finding rot, or as was the case with a recent White Maple project, planning to build an addition on an existing foundation only to realize the foundation doesn't have footings.

It's also hard to grow as a company doing less lucrative remodel jobs.

"Typically for us in the past if it's not a $100,000 or more job, we've not been able to be real competitive with the smaller companies," Rogers said. "And now we're having to try and make sure we're competitive."

data.title: Govt Tightens Extension Rules For 7 Pre-NELP Oil And Gas Blocks
data.description:
The revised framework sets higher government revenue shares during extended contract periods, requires minimum production or drilling performance, and mandates fresh reserves audits and investment commitments

The government has tightened the conditions for extending production-sharing contracts (PSCs) covering seven pre-New Exploration Licensing Policy (Pre-NELP) oil and gas blocks, introducing higher government profit shares, minimum performance requirements, and investment commitments for contractors.

Under the revised policy, notified by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas on 10 November, contract extensions can be granted in one or more instalments of up to 30 years each, subject to the continued commercial viability of the fields.

The government's share of profit petroleum will be increased by 10 percentage points over the rate calculated under normal PSC provisions during the first 10 years of an extension. The additional share will be five percentage points for the next 10 years and 2.5 percentage points for the following 10 years. Normal PSC provisions will apply thereafter.

The revised framework supersedes the policy issued in April 2017 and follows the notification of the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025, and the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025.

Eligibility Conditions Tightened

Contractors can apply for an extension after completing half of the original contract term or its extended term. Applications must be submitted at least two years before the contract expires.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) is required to make its recommendation within six months of receiving an application, while the government will decide within three months of receiving the proposal.

Applicants must establish that recoverable reserves remain in the field through a third-party reserves audit and submit a field development plan or revised plan covering the proposed extension period. This must include estimates of remaining reserves, projected production based on reservoir simulation studies, proposed work programmes and estimated expenditure.

For development areas with remaining recoverable 2P/P50 reserves exceeding five million barrels of oil equivalent, the reserves audit must be carried out by an internationally reputed consultant from a panel maintained by the DGH.

Contractors must also demonstrate satisfactory performance during the preceding 10 years. They must have either drilled at least 70 per cent of the development wells specified in the approved field development plan or achieved at least 70 per cent of committed production under the approved field operating plan or work programme.

Other requirements include clearing all statutory dues, demonstrating technical expertise, and complying with site restoration fund and site restoration plan obligations.

Investment And Government Safeguards

The revised policy requires contractors to furnish a bank guarantee equivalent to 10 per cent of the total estimated annual expenditure under the work programme approved by the Management Committee. A grace period of up to one year may be allowed for completing delayed work, subject to an extension of the bank guarantee and other conditions.

During the extended period, royalties and cess will be payable at prevailing rates applicable under the nomination regime, with contractors contributing in proportion to their participating interests.

The government has retained the option to invite fresh bids if contractors fail to meet the eligibility and performance requirements. It can also assign the fields to national oil companies, including Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India (OIL).

The government can refuse an extension without assigning reasons and impose additional conditions for individual contracts. Contractors unwilling to accept the revised policy will have their fields considered for rebidding on an as-is-where-is basis.

Seven Blocks Covered

The revised policy applies to seven blocks: RJ-ON-90/1 and SGL (RJ-ON/6) in Rajasthan; Dirok AAP-ON-94/1 and AA-ONJ/2 in Assam and Assam-Mizoram; and Tarapur (CB-ON/2), Palej-Pramoda (CB-ON/7) and CB-ON/3 in Gujarat.

Existing extensions granted under the 2017 policy will remain valid until their approved expiry dates. However, first-time extension applications beyond the original PSC term and applications for further extensions beyond currently approved periods will be governed by the revised framework.

The policy also allows contractors to choose the seat of arbitration in accordance with Rule 51 of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025.

data.title: Positive Health Awards Honour The Broken Who Transformed Into Beacons Of Hope
data.description:
Life can take away the ability to walk, the gift of speech, or a life free from pain. It cannot take away the courage to dream or the compassion to lift others

On the 17th of November, 2026, six extraordinary people who turned adversity into hope were honoured at the 18th Dr Batra's Positive Health Awards at the Jamshed Bhabha Theatre, NCPA, Mumbai. For Padma Shri Dr Mukesh Batra, the 18-year philanthropic journey celebrates people who turn suffering into purpose. It reminds society that healing goes beyond medicine to dignity, compassion and hope.

This Year's Positive Health Heroes Embody That Spirit:

Pratishtha Deveshwar was paralysed at 13. She became India's first wheelchair user to graduate from Oxford. Shrenik Shah lost his natural voice to cancer and has since inspired more than 100,000 people. Neha Bhatt lost a leg in an accident and rebuilt her life as an entrepreneur. Harishchandra Sude has spent four decades empowering persons with disabilities. Anil Kadian overcame polio to become India's fastest wheelchair marathoner.

Muhammad Aasim, born without arms, won international gold in para-swimming. Chief Guest Shri Ravi Kishan was joined by Rohit Roy, Zayed Khan, Amit Sadh, Esha Deol, Madhoo, Pooja Bedi and Anu Malik, with more than 1,100 guests in attendance.

“The human body may heal by medicine, but the human spirit heals itself, once it decides to,” said Dr Mukesh Batra. “When you live for others, your own pain loses its grip. The healthiest thing a human being can possess is hope. The final word belongs to the human spirit.”

Shri Ravi Kishan called the honourees “the real heroes of India” and saluted their courage. Past awardees include Arunima Sinha, who climbed Everest; Deepa Malik, who made Paralympic history; and acid-attack survivor Laxmi Agarwal, who walked an international fashion runway. Beyond the applause, the evening stood for a deeper truth: the greatest triumph is becoming the reason someone else finds the courage to rise. The awards were supported by Bajaj Auto Limited, Prestige, Fibe, and the Chinoy Foundation.

data.title: Celebrating Swastik Nigam: The Entrepreneur Making Global Finance More Accessible
data.description:
Nigam's journey reflects the ambition to make international finance more accessible to Indian businesses and individuals

As Swastik Nigam, Founder and CEO of Winvesta, celebrates his birthday today, it is an occasion to recognise an entrepreneurial journey shaped by global financial expertise, innovation and a commitment to simplifying international banking and investments.

An accomplished investment banker turned entrepreneur, Nigam has carved a distinctive path in the financial services industry. His career reflects a transition from managing complex financial portfolios at one of the world's leading banking institutions to building a technology-driven business addressing the challenges of cross-border transactions.

An alumnus of the prestigious Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIM-A), Nigam spent more than a decade in global finance. During his tenure as a Director at Deutsche Bank in London, he managed a multi-billion-euro global trading book spanning equities, exchange-traded funds, fixed income and currencies. The experience provided him with an understanding of international financial markets, investment strategies and the complexities of global banking.

However, it was his entrepreneurial ambition that eventually led him to establish Winvesta in 2019, alongside co-founder Prateek Jain.

Built around the idea of making financial borders less restrictive, Winvesta set out to simplify global banking, international investments and cross-border payments for Indian individuals and businesses. The platform addresses challenges traditionally associated with international financial transactions, including complicated banking processes, currency conversions and transaction costs.

Under Nigam's leadership, Winvesta has developed solutions offering multi-currency accounts, international payment capabilities and access to global investment opportunities. Its services are designed to support businesses, freelancers and individuals navigating an increasingly interconnected global economy.

The company's growth ambitions have attracted the attention of prominent investors, including CRED founder Kunal Shah, Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest and entrepreneur Umang Bedi. Their backing reflects investor interest in the opportunity to simplify international financial services through technology.

Beyond building Winvesta, Nigam has maintained an active association with the entrepreneurial and investment ecosystem. He has also served as Chair of the IIM Ahmedabad Alumni London Chapter, strengthening connections among professionals and business leaders.

What makes Nigam's professional journey particularly interesting is the combination of institutional banking experience and entrepreneurial thinking. Having worked within the established structures of global finance, he chose to address some of their inefficiencies through a technology-led venture.

At a time when Indian businesses are increasingly exploring international markets and individuals are seeking greater access to global financial opportunities, the relevance of accessible cross-border financial services continues to grow.

As Nigam celebrates another year, his journey stands as an example of how financial expertise, entrepreneurial ambition and technology can come together to address longstanding industry challenges.

data.title: China's steel sector bifurcates as iron ore remains robust: Russell
data.description:
By Clyde Russell

The contrasts in China's steel and iron ore sectors are continuing with ongoing weakness in steel output seemingly at odds with still robust imports of the key raw material.

China, which produces just over half of global steel, made 70.83 million metric tons in October, a daily rate of 2.28 million tons, according to official data released last week.

This was down 6.9% from the 2.45 million tons produced in September and 1.6% lower than the output in October 2025.

For the first 10 months of the year China's steel production was 795.61 million tons, a drop of 2.8% from the same period last year.

The overall picture is of a steel sector struggling for momentum amid weakness in property construction, one of the key end users that accounts for about one-third of demand.

But the pain isn't being evenly spread throughout China's vast steel sector.

China's blast furnaces were operating at 58% of capacity in early November, about 7 percentage points below normal for this time of year, according to data compiled by commodity analysts DBX Commodities.

But there is a large discrepancy between steel-producing regions, with blast furnaces in Hebei on the north coast operating at 70%, 6 percentage points above the 2020-2024 range, while those inland on the Yangtze belt were at 52%, 17 percentage points below the average, according to DBX.

DBX said that margins at steel mills across China halved between May and September, but it's the inland mills that are being forced to reduce output, with current production being down about 31 million tons on an annualised basis.

It's likely that northern coastal mills are able to keep running because it is easier for them to access export markets.

While China's steel exports are down 2.3% in the first 10 months of the year to 95.5 million tons, shipments for October were 9.85 million, up 0.7% from the 9.78 million for the same month last year.

The stronger operating rates for coastal mills are also drawing in higher volumes of metallurgical coal from the seaborne market, with DBX saying 7.2 million tons arrived in China in October, the highest in its records and up 47% from the same month last year.

IRON ORE RESILIENCE

While not as impressive as the gain in seaborne metallurgical coal, iron ore imports have held up better than the soft steel output numbers would suggest they should.

China's seaborne imports of iron ore are estimated at 116.4 million tons for November by commodity analysts Kpler, which would be up from the official customs figure of 105.66 million for October.

For the first 10 months of the year, customs data showed iron ore imports at 1.06 billion tons, up 3.1% from the corresponding period in 2025.

It is the case that much of the increase has been used to rebuild inventories, with port stockpiles (SH-TOT-IRONINV) rising to 157.36 million tons in the week to November 20, according to data compiled by consultants MySteel.

This is up 17.74 million tons, or 12.7%, from the 139.62 million recorded for the same week in 2025.

A declining trend in iron ore prices since May has helped keep demand strong, with the benchmark Singapore Exchange contract (SZZFc1) ending at $90.37 a ton on November 20, just up from the four-year low of $89.69 on November 17 and down 19.2% from the high so far this year of $111.91 on May 11.

Iron ore prices have eased this year amid plentiful supply from top exporters Australia and Brazil, as well as the gradual ramp-up in volumes from Guinea, home to the Simandou project.

China's imports from Guinea reached 3.12 million tons in October, according to Kpler data, and they are forecast to rise to 4.49 million in November and 5.75 million in December.

Gold prices rose in early Asian trade on Monday, recovering from the previous session's 14-month low, as investors positioned themselves for a key US inflation report that could offer clues on the Federal Reserve's next policy move.

FUNDAMENTALS

* Spot gold climbed 1.2% to $3,576.10 per ounce by 0048 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 on Friday. Bullion declined about 9% last week, its steepest weekly decline since March.

* US gold futures for December delivery gained 1.7% to $3,576.20.

* Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made a case on Friday for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank's current policy rate was not high enough to deal with inflation levels she viewed with "great concern."

* Energy-driven inflation pressures are significant, with rising natural gas prices a particular concern for policymakers, though it is not yet clear whether they have spread to the wider euro zone economy, European Central Bank Governing Council member Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Friday.

* Markets are currently pricing in a 93% chance of an interest rate hike at the central bank's policy meeting in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

* Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

* The US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate, is due on Wednesday.

* Elsewhere, physical gold demand in India and China picked up last week as prices fell, with bargain hunters flocking to stores in India and Chinese investors viewing the correction as an opportunity to accumulate bullion for investment.

data.title: 51Talk Student from Indonesia Takes the Stage at COP31 to Speak on Climate Change
data.description:
Athar shares his perspective on climate change at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, joining young participants from six countries on the global stage.

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Athar, a young student from Indonesia, took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share his thoughts on climate change and the future of the planet.

Speaking alongside young participants from Türkiye, China, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Thailand, Athar delivered his message in English, addressing the climate concerns, questions, and hopes of Indonesian children for a better environmental future. His participation demonstrated how children can use English to communicate their ideas and contribute to conversations that extend beyond their own communities.

Athar was among nine young participants from six countries supported by 51Talk, a global 1-on-1 online English education platform.

Since 2019, 51Talk has helped young learners share their perspectives at UN events, with COP31 marking the fifth time the company has brought young participants to speak on a UN stage.

Athar's Experience on the Global Stage

For Athar, 9, from Jakarta, participating in COP31 was an opportunity to speak about an issue that matters to him while experiencing what it means to address an international audience.

In his presentation, Athar shared his perspective on environmental responsibility, highlighting how small actions, such as reducing plastic waste and taking care of nature, can make a difference in protecting our planet. He encouraged listeners to take collective action for a healthier and more sustainable future for the next generation.

"I was a little nervous at first, but when I stood on the stage, I felt happy and proud. It was a great opportunity for me to share my thoughts and bring the perspectives of Indonesian children to the world," Athar said.

Ahead of the conference, Athar prepared for his speech through 51Talk's 1-on-1 online English lessons and dedicated speech practice, with support from his family. Working with his English teachers, he practiced organizing his thoughts and expressing his ideas clearly and confidently in English.

The experience also offered opportunities beyond public speaking. During his time in Antalya, Athar met young participants from different countries, exchanged ideas, and experienced firsthand how a shared language can bring people together.

"It was a special experience for me to meet people from different countries and share my thoughts about protecting our planet. I hope the questions I brought from Indonesian children can help more people listen to what children think about our future," Athar added.

Building Speaking Confidence Beyond the Classroom

At 51Talk, learning English is about more than developing language proficiency. It is also about helping children gain the confidence to express themselves and communicate in real-world situations.

51Talk combines personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers supported by professional training and teaching standards. Through interactive lessons and individualized guidance, children have regular opportunities to practice speaking, share opinions, and strengthen their communication skills.

Athar's participation at COP31 reflects this approach, showing how English learning can create opportunities for children to share their ideas on an international stage.

"Seeing Athar take part in COP31 is a proud moment for us. From his experience at the Global Youth Summit to this international climate conference, he continues to show that children can make meaningful contributions to important global conversations. We are glad to support his journey and see him take this opportunity to represent Indonesia," said Martin, General Manager of 51Talk Indonesia.

To further support practical communication skills, 51Talk introduced Global Communicator in 2026, a curriculum designed to connect English learning with real-world communication. Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, Global Communicator features immersive, task-based activities built around everyday situations and cross-cultural topics. AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help address individual learning needs and make progress more visible to families.

data.title: Half of wallets on Trump’s dinner list got tokens from non-US exchanges
data.description:
More than half the wallets that qualified for Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner on Sunday received TRUMP tokens from crypto exchanges that bar US users, according to analysis from consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

Trump is hosting his second dinner for his top memecoin holders at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, more than a year after an inaugural dinner in May 2025. The dinner offers up to 185 seats based on time-weighted TRUMP holdings.

Public Citizen said it traced 66 of the 130 wallets on the public leaderboard to exchanges including Binance (the global exchange), Bybit and BloFin — which are not permitted to serve US citizens. The list also included 15 of the 29 wallets that qualified for a VIP reception with the president.

“If those bans are enforced, many of the people vying for a seat at the president’s table don’t live in the United States,” said Public Citizen research director Zach Everson.

Trump’s memecoin events have drawn scrutiny over whether foreign buyers can essentially buy access to the president. Democratic lawmakers called on the White House to release the guest list for the first dinner in May 2025, while some joined a protest outside the golf club. They renewed the request again in October.

Who qualified for Trump’s memecoin dinner?

FastX, a Singapore-linked crypto trading platform, was the top-ranked wallet, holding $1.65 million in TRUMP at the time of the snapshot on Nov. 16.

The third highest ranked wallet has been linked to Unitas, a stablecoin issuer run by a British Virgin Islands company, according to Public Citizen.

Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands and founder and CEO of AirdropAlert, shared a picture from the Trump gala dinner on X. He came 26th with $45,351 in time-weighted TRUMP holdings.

Public Citizen also identified 14 wallets it suspects were controlled by the same person or group. Each received approximately 3,700 TRUMP tokens from Binance in October before being emptied weeks ahead of the cutoff.

Tron founder Justin Sun, the top-ranked holder at the May 2025 dinner, was expected to skip the event, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Meanwhile, Trump is a featured speaker for the event, and guests also include Floyd Mayweather, “Shark Tank” investor Kevin O’Leary, former NBA player Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Suchard.

Trump token down 99% from peak

The gala dinner comes even as the TRUMP token trades 98.8% below its all-time high of $75.35.

Trump held the first dinner for TRUMP holders in May 2025 at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, when the token was trading at $14.43. By the time he held his second memecoin event, a conference and luncheon at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, the token had already dropped to $2.88.

As of the time of writing, the TRUMP token is trading at $0.89.

data.title: Libya's NOC says 'unlawful' pipeline closure from Sharara oilfield to cut output by 350,000 bpd
data.description:
Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said on Monday the closure of a valve on a pipeline from the Sharara oilfield, one of Libya's largest, by an "unlawful group" would result in the loss of around 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) of production.

A second pipeline, linking the Hamada field to the country's largest refinery, Zawiya, has also remained closed for more than two weeks, resulting in the loss of around 15,000 bpd, the NOC said, bringing Libya's total oil production losses to approximately 365,000 bpd.

The NOC said in October that an armed group had shut a valve on the main Hamada crude oil pipeline, halting flows. The Corporation said on Saturday that the forced closure of the Hamada oil pipeline had cost the country more than $30.8 million, renewing its condemnation of attacks on oil facilities.

Located ​in southwestern Libya, Sharara ​is operated ⁠by a joint venture of the state-owned NOC via Acacus oil company with Spain's Repsol , France's TotalEnergies , Austria's ​OMV and Norway's Equinor .

Libyan oil output has been subject to repeated closures for political ​and technical reasons since the 2011 uprising against Muammar Gaddafi.

Oil production is Libya's main economic resource, representing ​approximately 90% ⁠of its economy.

data.title: Axel REE Appoints WSP Australia to Conduct Woolrich ISR Field Program
data.description:
Axel REE has appointed global engineering consultancy WSP Australia to lead the technical studies, planning, design, and execution of the Woolrich deposit in situ recovery (ISR) field program within its Caladão rare earth-gallium project in Brazil.

WSP’s expertise will support the integration of hydrogeological and potential geotechnical investigations into the design and implementation of the program, which will evaluate the behaviour of magnesium sulphate ISR under certain field conditions.

These will include solution migration through the mineralised regolith, hydraulic containment, and the recovery of rare earth-bearing pregnant leach solution (PLS).

Axel is now advancing the remaining technical and operational activities required for field program execution, including completion of auger drilling, integration of leach results from SGS Laboratories, and advancing WSP’s specialist investigations.

Priority ISR Deposit

Woolrich, which is Axel’s priority deposit for the development and field validation of its proposed magnesium sulphate ISR process, hosts a mineral resource of 264.6 million tonnes at 1,101 parts per million total rare earth oxides (TREO) including a maiden 110.1Mt indicated resource at 1,073ppm TREO.

It is one of four defined rare earth deposits within the Caladão project, which hosts a global resource of 708.6Mt at 1,443ppm TREO.

Axel recently secured environmental and water clearances for the start of the ISR program and is confirming municipal requirements for other authorisations such as approvals relating to permanent preservation areas or vegetation clearance.

It will test whether the leaching response demonstrated in earlier column work can be repeated consistently in the ground while also examining hydraulic response, operating parameters and the behaviour of the mineralised profile at larger scale.

Site-Specific Data

Managing director Dr Patience Mpofu said Axel expected the results of the WSP study to provide site-specific operating data to guide future wellfield design and the evaluation of potential larger-scale ISR operations.

“Following our recent success in producing high-grade mixed rare earth carbonate from laboratory-scale leach solutions, our next priority is to evaluate the performance of magnesium sulphate ISR under field conditions,” she said.

“This program will provide critical technical information to support our strategy to unlock the potential of the Woolrich rare earth deposit.”

In parallel with the WSP appointment, Axel has commenced a detailed auger drilling program within the designated 20,000-square-metre study area at Woolrich to improve the geological definition of the mineralised regolith and generate additional samples for magnesium sulphate leach testing.

The systematic data-driven approach will support the final design for the field program and provide a stronger technical foundation for evaluating the performance of magnesium sulphate ISR under representative site conditions.
